chapter_theme: The last ten charanams of Kaduveli's Anandakkalippu: a run of prohibitions (keep no company with revilers, do not lie though the world lies, do not stone birds, do not play with snakes, do not smoke ganja or drink, do not put on false guises or wash obligations away in Gangas), then the positive close: set up the ladder of bhakti and drive off the sects, discern eight-limbed yoga and rebuke lust, know the many castes as one, and the Lord as the self-luminous one who dwells in lovers' hearts and calls himself the servant of his servants.
structure_note: 1565 to 1569 and 1573 are prohibitions in the ஆதே form; 1570 to 1572 are commands (bhakti as ladder, discernment and ashtanga yoga, all castes one); 1574 ends the song with a description of the Lord rather than counsel to the mind.

1565.reading: Do not keep company with those who revile; though this whole world should lie, do not lie; do not do cruel deeds; do not shoot stones at birds for nothing.
1565.nuance: The last line is the song's most concrete: idle stone-throwing at birds, a boy's cruelty, stands for all needless harm. Truth is set against the whole world's falsehood, not against convenience.

1566.reading: Desire nothing but Siva; do not stir up a quarrel harmful to anyone into a blaze; do not leap out of the state of tapas; do not want a book that lacks the good path.
1566.nuance: சன்மார்க்கம் இல்லாத நூல் is a book without the true path, which matches 1564's 'false Veda' and 1569's 'books of ignorance without bhakti': the song judges texts by whether they teach devotion and the path, not by canon.

1567.reading: Do not catch a snake and make it dance; do not disgrace your wives and show it; do not feed the world neem; do not plant your vainglory where it shows.
1567.nuance: On the plain reading the snake is a snake-charmer's show, one of the fraud-tricks the Siddhars list; tradition also hears the serpent of the body, the coiled power, not to be toyed with for display. வேம்பு, neem, is bitterness given to others, perhaps harsh words. பத்தினிமார் in the plural is odd for one man's wives and may mean chaste women generally.

1568.reading: Do not go near the ritual that people praise; do not let yourself be spoken of with praise among the many; do not count up your life as you proclaim it; do not make lowness so that others fall.
1568.nuance: சாற்றும் உன் வாழ்வை எண்ணாதே is unclear: do not reckon your life as something to announce, or do not think of the life you boast of. The first line rejects சடங்கு, ceremony, as such, which goes further than 1555's rejection of pilgrimage.

1569.reading: Do not smoke ganja; do not drink the liquor that shows madness and stupefies; do not kill lives so that they tremble; do not read the books of ignorance that have no bhakti.
1569.nuance: The Siddhars were accused of using hemp and opium, and Sivavakkiyar's catalogue of frauds confirms that some did; Kaduveli's prohibition is from inside the tradition. அஞ்ச உயிர் மடியாதே: do not take lives so that they fear, or do not die in fear; the former fits the list of harms.

1570.reading: Setting up the ladder called bhakti, stretching it to the place seen to be free of the bonds of pairs, gathering what is called truth, daily make it your own, driving the sects away.
1570.nuance: தொந்த பந்தம், the bond of dvandva, the pairs (pleasure and pain, heat and cold), names what the ladder climbs out of. சமயங்கள் ஓட்டி, driving off the sects, sets bhakti itself above sectarian religion, a Siddhar commonplace put here as the last rung.

1571.reading: All the many kinds of lust, past telling: cry fie on them, rebuke them, and take firm discernment; the incomparable eight-limbed yoga, discern it well and know it; the truth of those is enjoyment.
1571.nuance: அவற்று உண்மை சம்போகம், the truth of them is enjoyment, is a striking end: the word for sexual union is used for the fruit of yoga and discernment, after lust has been spat at in the first line. The song does not spell out the eight limbs.

1572.reading: Every kind of good justice, know them all, take them up and teach them; the many castes said not to agree, know every one of them as one, realise it, and declare it as kinship.
1572.nuance: உறவு ஓதி, declaring kinship, makes the oneness of castes something to be taught, not only held. The song's own use of சண்டாளம் as a name for anger in 1548 shows how far the caste vocabulary persists even in the poet who says this.

1573.reading: Do not put on a false guise; do not go wetting your obligations in many Gangas; do not think of plunder; having made a friendship, do not turn to tale-bearing.
1573.nuance: கடன் நனையாதே puts debts or duties into the river: the pilgrim bathes to discharge what he owes. பல கங்கை, many Gangas, mocks the multiplication of holy rivers. The false guise and the bathing stand together as the two public forms of religious pretence.

1574.reading: The self-luminous one is everywhere; he dwells in the joyful heart of lovers; he is the servant of the pure devotees; if one praises him, the Lord grants one's state.
1574.nuance: அடியவர் தாசன், servant of the servants, reverses the order of lord and devotee, a bhakti figure the song saves for its last stanza. சுயபிரகாசன், self-luminous, is the Vedantic name for the Self, placed beside the devotional one without comment.

links.note: Sivavakkiyar asks when he will stop drinking ganja, opium and toddy and drink the five-fold nectar instead; Kaduveli tells the mind not to smoke ganja or drink the liquor that stupefies. Both renounce the drugs from within the Siddhar tradition; Sivavakkiyar names the inner nectar as the replacement, Kaduveli leaves it to 1563.

Sivavakkiyar describes frauds who smoke ganja at set hours and eat opium to be esteemed as kaya-kalpa men, roaming like dogs; Kaduveli forbids ganja and liquor outright. Sivavakkiyar's is a portrait of the abusers, Kaduveli's a rule for the hearer; together they show the drugs were a live problem among the Siddhars' own.

Tirumular makes the thirty-six tattvas the rungs of a ladder to release, climbed into the inner light; Kaduveli sets up a ladder called bhakti and stretches it to the place free of the pairs. The same ladder, but the rungs differ: Tirumular's are the constituents of the world known in order, Kaduveli's a single devotion that also drives off the sects.

Tirumular lists the eight limbs, yama, niyama, postures, breath control, withdrawal, concentration, meditation and samadhi; Kaduveli only tells the mind to discern the incomparable eight-limbed yoga well, and adds that its truth is enjoyment. Kaduveli presupposes Tirumular's list and adds a judgement on its fruit.

Sivavakkiyar asks when he will reach the thing that lies beyond eight-limbed yoga and beyond what is beyond it; Kaduveli commends eight-limbed yoga as the thing to discern and know. Not a contradiction, since Kaduveli does not call it final, but Sivavakkiyar's stanza marks the limit of what Kaduveli recommends.

The Kural says birth is alike for all beings and distinction comes only from the difference in what they do; Kaduveli tells the mind to know the many castes said to be unequal as one and declare it as kinship. Both deny difference by birth; the Kural keeps a difference by work, Kaduveli names none.

Tirumular says that for those who set Nandi in love by knowledge there is no impurity, no pride, no caste and no good to seek; Kaduveli asks the hearer to know all castes as one and teach it. Tirumular's casteless state is the knower's condition; Kaduveli's is a truth to be realised and preached.

The Kural says many with impurity in their minds bathe as though distinguished and go about concealed; Kaduveli says not to put on a false guise or wet one's obligations in many Gangas. Both pair ritual bathing with concealment: the bath is the disguise.

1555 asks whether Kasi and the Ganga remove karma; 1573 turns the question into a rule and sets the bathing beside the false guise and plunder. The second stanza treats pilgrimage not as useless but as a kind of fraud.

source_issues: 1574: துதுக்கிற் is a miscopy for துதிக்கிற் (if one praises).
